html:
SMTO-SKL-0068 — The next page of Microsoft 365 results has expired

GUID: 2baabe49-7a9f-50fb-9dd8-56b803ecfd29
Slug: microsoft365-cursor-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO was fetching more results from an earlier Microsoft 365 search, but that search is too old, SMTO restarted, or the search details changed. Nothing in your account was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to repeat the whole search, for example "search my inbox again for invoices from March". A fresh search starts over and gets new, valid page links.
  2. Ask for the next pages soon after, without changing the account or the search words in between. SMTO's page links expire after 15 minutes and only work for the exact same search.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the first page of results again and can continue to the next pages.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 continuation cursor was missing, expired (15 minutes or a Server restart) or bound to a different account, operation or query.

What this means

  • An opaque continuation handle is missing, expired or bound to different account/operation/query evidence. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • An opaque continuation handle is missing, expired or bound to different account/operation/query evidence.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current binding and query with the original cursor; handles expire after 15 minutes or restart.

How to fix it

  • Continuation handles live in process memory for 15 minutes and are bound to account, operation and arguments (Handles.get in skills/microsoft365/client.py). Restart the read from the first page with the same account_ref and filters and page through without changing them; handles do not survive a Server restart.
  • Restart the bounded read with identical account and filters. Continuations expire after 15 minutes or a service restart.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A new bounded read uses the intended same account and filters.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
